es-cava-comtats-de-barcelona.name: Comtats de Barcelona
es-cava-comtats-de-barcelona.grapes: Macabeo, Xarel·lo, Parellada, Chardonnay; Trepat, Garnacha, Monastrell and Pinot Noir for rosé
es-cava-comtats-de-barcelona.classification: Zona of DO Cava (zoning approved 2020, on labels from 2022): one of four zones, which can appear on labels of Cava de Guarda Superior and above.
es-cava-comtats-de-barcelona.summary:
Comtats de Barcelona ('the counties of Barcelona') is the Catalan heart of Cava, covering the great majority of production, with the town of Sant Sadurní d'Anoia in the Penedès as its capital. Its five subzones are Valls d'Anoia-Foix, Serra de Mar, Conca del Gaià, Serra de Prades and Pla de Ponent. Macabeo, Xarel·lo and Parellada are the classic trio, Xarel·lo giving body and longevity.

Codorníu, which made Spain's first traditional-method sparkling wine in 1872, and Freixenet are based in Sant Sadurní, as are Juvé & Camps and Recaredo. Some of the best growers have left the DO: Raventós i Blanc in 2012 to create Conca del Riu Anoia, and Gramona, Recaredo and others in 2019 to form Corpinnat.
es-cava-comtats-de-barcelona.terroir: Limestone, clay and sandy soils from the Mediterranean coast to the inland plateau.

es-cava-levante.name: Levante
es-cava-levante.classification: Zona of DO Cava (zoning approved 2020, on labels from 2022): one of four zones, which can appear on labels of Cava de Guarda Superior and above.
es-cava-levante.summary: The Levante zone is Requena, on the high plateau west of Valencia at about 600 to 900 m, a continental climate with cold nights that keep acidity in Macabeo and Chardonnay. Requena is the second-largest Cava area after Catalonia; Dominio de la Vega, Pago de Tharsys and Hispano-Suizas are among its producers.
es-cava-levante.terroir: High continental plateau of Requena with limestone and clay soils.

es-cava-valle-del-ebro.name: Valle del Ebro
es-cava-valle-del-ebro.classification: Zona of DO Cava (zoning approved 2020, on labels from 2022): one of four zones, which can appear on labels of Cava de Guarda Superior and above.
es-cava-valle-del-ebro.summary: The Valle del Ebro zone gathers the Cava municipalities of La Rioja, Álava, Navarra and Aragón (Zaragoza and Huesca) along the Ebro valley, with two subzones, Alto Ebro and Valle del Cierzo, the latter named after the cold north-west wind of Aragón. Macabeo (Viura) is the main grape, and several Rioja houses make Cava, among them Muga, whose Conde de Haro is one of the best known.

es-cava-vinedos-de-almendralejo.name: Viñedos de Almendralejo
es-cava-vinedos-de-almendralejo.classification: Zona of DO Cava (zoning approved 2020, on labels from 2022): one of four zones, which can appear on labels of Cava de Guarda Superior and above.
es-cava-vinedos-de-almendralejo.summary: A small, isolated Cava zone around Almendralejo in Extremadura, in the province of Badajoz, on the flat Tierra de Barros plain at about 300 m. Macabeo and Parellada dominate; Bodegas Vía de la Plata is the best-known producer, and the zone shows how Cava's rules follow a production method rather than a single region.
es-cava-vinedos-de-almendralejo.terroir: Flat, red clay plain of the Tierra de Barros.

es-priorat-bellmunt-del-priorat.name: Bellmunt del Priorat
es-priorat-bellmunt-del-priorat.grapes: Garnacha and Cariñena (at least 60% together), with Garnacha Blanca for white
es-priorat-bellmunt-del-priorat.classification: Vi de vila of DOQ Priorat: one of 12 village zones (2009 rules). Grapes from that zone only, yield at most 5,000 kg/ha for red, at least 60% Garnacha and/or Cariñena.
es-priorat-bellmunt-del-priorat.summary: A village in the south of the DOQ, the lowest and warmest part of the area, once a lead-mining centre whose mine is now a museum. Its vineyards mix llicorella with other soils and give ripe, generous wines; Mas d'en Gil is based here.
es-priorat-bellmunt-del-priorat.terroir: The mapped village area lies at about 105 to 325 m, with a mean slope of about 27% (Copernicus DEM).

es-priorat-el-lloar.name: El Lloar
es-priorat-el-lloar.grapes: Garnacha and Cariñena (at least 60% together), with Garnacha Blanca for white
es-priorat-el-lloar.classification: Vi de vila of DOQ Priorat: one of 12 village zones (2009 rules). Grapes from that zone only, yield at most 5,000 kg/ha for red, at least 60% Garnacha and/or Cariñena.
es-priorat-el-lloar.summary: A small village perched above the Siurana river in the west of the DOQ, with steep llicorella slopes falling to the river. Its wines share the dark, mineral character of the Siurana valley.
es-priorat-el-lloar.terroir: The mapped village area lies at about 160 to 460 m, with a mean slope of about 32% (Copernicus DEM).

es-priorat-escaladei.name: Escaladei
es-priorat-escaladei.grapes: Garnacha and Cariñena (at least 60% together), with Garnacha Blanca for white
es-priorat-escaladei.classification: Vi de vila of DOQ Priorat: one of 12 village zones (2009 rules). Grapes from that zone only, yield at most 5,000 kg/ha for red, at least 60% Garnacha and/or Cariñena.
es-priorat-escaladei.summary: The hamlet beside the Cartoixa d'Escaladei, the first Carthusian monastery of the Iberian Peninsula, founded in 1194 below the cliffs of the Montsant. The monks planted the vineyards that gave the Priorat (the 'priory') its name and ran the region until the monastery was dissolved in 1835. The vineyards here are among the highest of the DOQ, with fresher Garnatxa; Scala Dei is the historic winery.
es-priorat-escaladei.terroir: The mapped village area lies at about 395 to 970 m, with a mean slope of about 38% (Copernicus DEM).
es-priorat-escaladei.nerd_note: Escaladei means 'ladder of God', from the legend of a shepherd who saw angels climbing a ladder to heaven from a pine tree here.

es-priorat-gratallops.name: Gratallops
es-priorat-gratallops.grapes: Garnacha and Cariñena (at least 60% together), with Garnacha Blanca for white
es-priorat-gratallops.classification: Vi de vila of DOQ Priorat: one of 12 village zones (2009 rules). Grapes from that zone only, yield at most 5,000 kg/ha for red, at least 60% Garnacha and/or Cariñena.
es-priorat-gratallops.summary:
Gratallops is where modern Priorat began. In 1989 René Barbier, Álvaro Palacios, Carles Pastrana, Josep Lluís Pérez and Daphne Glorian pooled their grapes in the village to make the first 'Clos' wines, and within a decade Clos Mogador, Clos Erasmus, Clos de l'Obac and Palacios's L'Ermita and Finca Dofí had made Priorat world-famous. The village sits on a ridge above the Siurana river, surrounded by steep terraces of *llicorella*, the dark, crumbling slate that forces vines to root deep and gives the wines their mineral grip.

Old Garnatxa and Carinyena, often blended with Syrah and Cabernet in the early years, give dense, warm wines with a stony, graphite edge.
es-priorat-gratallops.terroir: Steep llicorella (slate) terraces above the Siurana. The mapped village area lies at about 150 to 340 m, with a mean slope of about 29% (Copernicus DEM).
es-priorat-gratallops.nerd_note: Álvaro Palacios's L'Ermita, from a steep slope of old Garnatxa, is one of Spain's most expensive wines.

es-priorat-la-morera-de-montsant.name: La Morera de Montsant
es-priorat-la-morera-de-montsant.grapes: Garnacha and Cariñena (at least 60% together), with Garnacha Blanca for white
es-priorat-la-morera-de-montsant.classification: Vi de vila of DOQ Priorat: one of 12 village zones (2009 rules). Grapes from that zone only, yield at most 5,000 kg/ha for red, at least 60% Garnacha and/or Cariñena.
es-priorat-la-morera-de-montsant.summary: The highest village of the DOQ, below the limestone cliffs of the Serra de Montsant, with vineyards reaching well above 600 m. The altitude gives cooler nights and fresher, more aromatic wines than the warm valleys. The municipality also contains Escaladei, a separate vi de vila zone.
es-priorat-la-morera-de-montsant.terroir: The mapped village area lies at about 425 to 1095 m, with a mean slope of about 40% (Copernicus DEM).

es-priorat-la-vilella-alta.name: La Vilella Alta
es-priorat-la-vilella-alta.grapes: Garnacha and Cariñena (at least 60% together), with Garnacha Blanca for white
es-priorat-la-vilella-alta.classification: Vi de vila of DOQ Priorat: one of 12 village zones (2009 rules). Grapes from that zone only, yield at most 5,000 kg/ha for red, at least 60% Garnacha and/or Cariñena.
es-priorat-la-vilella-alta.summary: A small village in the centre of the DOQ, on the slopes above the Montsant river, with old vineyards on llicorella. Mas Alta is based here.
es-priorat-la-vilella-alta.terroir: The mapped village area lies at about 265 to 480 m, with a mean slope of about 34% (Copernicus DEM).

es-priorat-la-vilella-baixa.name: La Vilella Baixa
es-priorat-la-vilella-baixa.grapes: Garnacha and Cariñena (at least 60% together), with Garnacha Blanca for white
es-priorat-la-vilella-baixa.classification: Vi de vila of DOQ Priorat: one of 12 village zones (2009 rules). Grapes from that zone only, yield at most 5,000 kg/ha for red, at least 60% Garnacha and/or Cariñena.
es-priorat-la-vilella-baixa.summary: A village squeezed into a narrow gorge where the Montsant river meets a tributary, nicknamed 'the little New York of the Priorat' for its tall, narrow houses. Its vineyards climb the llicorella slopes above.
es-priorat-la-vilella-baixa.terroir: The mapped village area lies at about 195 to 410 m, with a mean slope of about 33% (Copernicus DEM).

es-priorat-masos-de-falset.name: Masos de Falset
es-priorat-masos-de-falset.grapes: Garnacha and Cariñena (at least 60% together), with Garnacha Blanca for white
es-priorat-masos-de-falset.classification: Vi de vila of DOQ Priorat: one of 12 village zones (2009 rules). Grapes from that zone only, yield at most 5,000 kg/ha for red, at least 60% Garnacha and/or Cariñena.
es-priorat-masos-de-falset.summary: The part of Falset that belongs to the DOQ Priorat, around the scattered farmhouses (*masos*) north of the town; the rest of Falset, the capital of the Priorat comarca, is in DO Montsant. Its vineyards sit on llicorella at the southern edge of the DOQ.
es-priorat-masos-de-falset.terroir: The mapped village area lies at about 200 to 535 m, with a mean slope of about 32% (Copernicus DEM).

es-priorat-poboleda.name: Poboleda
es-priorat-poboleda.grapes: Garnacha and Cariñena (at least 60% together), with Garnacha Blanca for white
es-priorat-poboleda.classification: Vi de vila of DOQ Priorat: one of 12 village zones (2009 rules). Grapes from that zone only, yield at most 5,000 kg/ha for red, at least 60% Garnacha and/or Cariñena.
es-priorat-poboleda.summary: Poboleda sits in the upper Siurana valley at the foot of the Montsant cliffs, in the north of the DOQ, where the llicorella slopes are a little higher and cooler. Mas Doix, whose old-vine Carinyena from Poboleda is a reference, is based here.
es-priorat-poboleda.terroir: The mapped village area lies at about 320 to 635 m, with a mean slope of about 34% (Copernicus DEM).

es-priorat-porrera.name: Porrera
es-priorat-porrera.grapes: Garnacha and Cariñena (at least 60% together), with Garnacha Blanca for white
es-priorat-porrera.classification: Vi de vila of DOQ Priorat: one of 12 village zones (2009 rules). Grapes from that zone only, yield at most 5,000 kg/ha for red, at least 60% Garnacha and/or Cariñena.
es-priorat-porrera.summary:
Porrera lies in a deep valley in the north-east of the DOQ, a village of old Carinyena vineyards on steep llicorella slopes. Its wines are often fresher and more aromatic than those of the warm Siurana valley, with Carinyena's acidity and a dark, mineral core.

Vall Llach, founded by the singer Lluís Llach, Sangenís i Vaqué and the Cims de Porrera project are based here.
es-priorat-porrera.terroir: Steep llicorella slopes in a deep valley; old Carinyena vines. The mapped village area lies at about 260 to 670 m, with a mean slope of about 38% (Copernicus DEM).

es-priorat-solanes-del-molar.name: Solanes del Molar
es-priorat-solanes-del-molar.summary: The sunny slopes (*solanes*) of El Molar in the south-west of the DOQ Priorat, the only part of that municipality inside the DOQ and one of its 12 vi de vila zones. It has no drawn boundary here because no open map of the zone exists.
es-priorat-solanes-del-molar.classification: Vi de vila of DOQ Priorat: one of 12 village zones (2009 rules). Not drawn on the map (no boundary available).

es-priorat-torroja-del-priorat.name: Torroja del Priorat
es-priorat-torroja-del-priorat.grapes: Garnacha and Cariñena (at least 60% together), with Garnacha Blanca for white
es-priorat-torroja-del-priorat.classification: Vi de vila of DOQ Priorat: one of 12 village zones (2009 rules). Grapes from that zone only, yield at most 5,000 kg/ha for red, at least 60% Garnacha and/or Cariñena.
es-priorat-torroja-del-priorat.summary: A hilltop village in the centre of the DOQ, surrounded by steep llicorella terraces and old vines. Dominik Huber's Terroir al Límit, which made lighter, whole-bunch, less extracted wines here from the mid-2000s, changed ideas of what Priorat could taste like.
es-priorat-torroja-del-priorat.terroir: The mapped village area lies at about 255 to 510 m, with a mean slope of about 32% (Copernicus DEM).

es-rioja-abalos.name: Ábalos
es-rioja-abalos.grapes: Tempranillo, Garnacha, Graciano, Mazuelo, Viura and others
es-rioja-abalos.classification: Vino de municipio of DOCa Rioja: since 2017 a wine may name its municipality if all the grapes come from it and it is made there.
es-rioja-abalos.summary: Ábalos is a municipality of Rioja Alta in La Rioja, on the north bank of the Ebro in the Sonsierra, below the Sierra de Cantabria, about 10 km west of Laguardia. Its land spans roughly 490 to 970 m. In Rioja Alta, the coolest and most Atlantic of the three zones, Tempranillo dominates on clay-limestone and alluvial soils. Puelles, a family estate, is based in the village. Recognised viñedos singulares include Puelles Zenus, Laderas del Portillo and La Artesilla de Leza García.

es-rioja-agoncillo.name: Agoncillo
es-rioja-agoncillo.grapes: Tempranillo, Garnacha, Graciano, Mazuelo, Viura and others
es-rioja-agoncillo.classification: Vino de municipio of DOCa Rioja: since 2017 a wine may name its municipality if all the grapes come from it and it is made there.
es-rioja-agoncillo.summary: Agoncillo is a municipality of Rioja Oriental in La Rioja, on the Ebro east of Logroño. Its land spans roughly 340 to 470 m. In the Mediterranean-influenced Rioja Oriental, Tempranillo and Garnacha ripen fully, giving generous, supple wines.

es-rioja-aguilar-del-rio-alhama.name: Aguilar del Río Alhama
es-rioja-aguilar-del-rio-alhama.grapes: Tempranillo, Garnacha, Graciano, Mazuelo, Viura and others
es-rioja-aguilar-del-rio-alhama.classification: Vino de municipio of DOCa Rioja: since 2017 a wine may name its municipality if all the grapes come from it and it is made there.
es-rioja-aguilar-del-rio-alhama.summary: Aguilar del Río Alhama is a municipality of Rioja Oriental in La Rioja, in the upper Alhama valley, about 30 km south of Arnedo. Its land spans roughly 610 to 1000 m. In the Mediterranean-influenced Rioja Oriental, Tempranillo and Garnacha ripen fully, giving generous, supple wines.

es-rioja-alavesa.name: Rioja Alavesa
es-rioja-alavesa.grapes: Tempranillo, Garnacha, Graciano, Mazuelo, Viura and others
es-rioja-alavesa.classification: Zona of DOCa Rioja: one of three zones that may appear on labels (rules of 2017, labels from 2018), for wines made entirely from grapes of that zone.
es-rioja-alavesa.summary:
Rioja Alavesa is the smallest zone: 15 municipalities of the Basque province of Álava on the north bank of the Ebro, on terraces and slopes that climb from the river toward the limestone wall of the Sierra de Cantabria. The sierra shelters the vineyards from cold northern winds, and the soils are pale, chalky clay-limestone, giving Tempranillo of fine acidity, perfume and finesse.

Alavesa has two traditions: the young, carbonic-maceration *vino de cosechero* of small family growers, and the estate wines that made its name, from Marqués de Riscal in Elciego (1858) to Remírez de Ganuza, Remelluri and Ysios. Its growers have pushed hardest for village and single-vineyard labelling, and almost half of Rioja's viñedos singulares are in Álava.
es-rioja-alavesa.terroir: Chalky clay-limestone on terraces below the Sierra de Cantabria; vineyards from about 400 m to over 700 m.

es-rioja-albelda-de-iregua.name: Albelda de Iregua
es-rioja-albelda-de-iregua.grapes: Tempranillo, Garnacha, Graciano, Mazuelo, Viura and others
es-rioja-albelda-de-iregua.classification: Vino de municipio of DOCa Rioja: since 2017 a wine may name its municipality if all the grapes come from it and it is made there.
es-rioja-albelda-de-iregua.summary: Albelda de Iregua is a municipality of Rioja Oriental in La Rioja, in the Iregua valley, about 11 km south of Logroño. Its land spans roughly 470 to 890 m. Rioja Oriental is warmer and drier, with Garnacha as the traditional grape and Tempranillo now dominant. The monastery of San Martín de Albelda produced the tenth-century Codex Albeldensis, one of the great manuscripts of medieval Spain.

es-rioja-alberite.name: Alberite
es-rioja-alberite.grapes: Tempranillo, Garnacha, Graciano, Mazuelo, Viura and others
es-rioja-alberite.classification: Vino de municipio of DOCa Rioja: since 2017 a wine may name its municipality if all the grapes come from it and it is made there.
es-rioja-alberite.summary: Alberite is a municipality of Rioja Oriental in La Rioja, in the lower Iregua valley, about 8 km south-east of Logroño. Its land spans roughly 430 to 540 m. Rioja Oriental is warmer and drier, with Garnacha as the traditional grape and Tempranillo now dominant.

es-rioja-alcanadre.name: Alcanadre
es-rioja-alcanadre.grapes: Tempranillo, Garnacha, Graciano, Mazuelo, Viura and others
es-rioja-alcanadre.classification: Vino de municipio of DOCa Rioja: since 2017 a wine may name its municipality if all the grapes come from it and it is made there.
es-rioja-alcanadre.summary: Alcanadre is a municipality of Rioja Oriental in La Rioja, on the Ebro, about 20 km north of Arnedo. Its land spans roughly 320 to 500 m. Rioja Oriental is warmer and drier, with Garnacha as the traditional grape and Tempranillo now dominant.

es-rioja-aldeanueva-de-ebro.name: Aldeanueva de Ebro
es-rioja-aldeanueva-de-ebro.grapes: Tempranillo, Garnacha, Graciano, Mazuelo, Viura and others
es-rioja-aldeanueva-de-ebro.classification: Vino de municipio of DOCa Rioja: since 2017 a wine may name its municipality if all the grapes come from it and it is made there.
es-rioja-aldeanueva-de-ebro.summary: Aldeanueva de Ebro is a municipality of Rioja Oriental in La Rioja, on the terraces below the Sierra de Yerga, about 10 km south-east of Calahorra. Its land spans roughly 290 to 490 m. Rioja Oriental is warmer and drier, with Garnacha as the traditional grape and Tempranillo now dominant. Recognised viñedos singulares include Canterabuey, Coscojares, 1890 Manzanos and Real Rubio Finca El Tordillo.

es-rioja-alesanco.name: Alesanco
es-rioja-alesanco.grapes: Tempranillo, Garnacha, Graciano, Mazuelo, Viura and others
es-rioja-alesanco.classification: Vino de municipio of DOCa Rioja: since 2017 a wine may name its municipality if all the grapes come from it and it is made there.
es-rioja-alesanco.summary: Alesanco is a municipality of Rioja Alta in La Rioja, on the plain west of Nájera. Its land spans roughly 550 to 660 m. Its vineyards share the Atlantic-influenced climate of Rioja Alta, which favours long-lived, fresh Tempranillo.

es-rioja-aleson.name: Alesón
es-rioja-aleson.grapes: Tempranillo, Garnacha, Graciano, Mazuelo, Viura and others
es-rioja-aleson.classification: Vino de municipio of DOCa Rioja: since 2017 a wine may name its municipality if all the grapes come from it and it is made there.
es-rioja-aleson.summary: Alesón is a municipality of Rioja Alta in La Rioja, in the Najerilla valley east of Nájera. Its land spans roughly 550 to 660 m. In Rioja Alta, the coolest and most Atlantic of the three zones, Tempranillo dominates on clay-limestone and alluvial soils.

es-rioja-alfaro.name: Alfaro
es-rioja-alfaro.grapes: Tempranillo, Garnacha, Graciano, Mazuelo, Viura and others
es-rioja-alfaro.classification: Vino de municipio of DOCa Rioja: since 2017 a wine may name its municipality if all the grapes come from it and it is made there.
es-rioja-alfaro.summary: Alfaro is a municipality of Rioja Oriental in La Rioja, at the eastern tip of the DOCa, between the Ebro and the Sierra de Yerga. Its land spans roughly 270 to 750 m. Rioja Oriental is warmer and drier, with Garnacha as the traditional grape and Tempranillo now dominant. The collegiate church of San Miguel carries one of Europe's largest colonies of white storks on a single building. Palacios Remondo, the family estate run by Álvaro Palacios since 2000, showed the potential of the high, cool Garnacha vineyards of the Sierra de Yerga. Recognised viñedos singulares include El Sueño de Amado, Planas Altas, Quiñón de Valmira, Lar de Sotomayor, Domeco de Jarauta, Laderas de Tambarría and Queirón Las Engalladas.

es-rioja-alta.name: Rioja Alta
es-rioja-alta.grapes: Tempranillo, Garnacha, Graciano, Mazuelo, Viura and others
es-rioja-alta.classification: Zona of DOCa Rioja: one of three zones that may appear on labels (rules of 2017, labels from 2018), for wines made entirely from grapes of that zone.
es-rioja-alta.summary:
Rioja Alta is the western and highest of Rioja's three zones: 76 municipalities of La Rioja (plus the Burgos enclave of El Ternero) on the south bank of the Ebro from Haro to Logroño and up the valleys of the Tirón, Oja, Najerilla and Iregua, with most vineyards between about 450 and 700 m. The climate has the strongest Atlantic influence in the region: cooler, wetter and later-ripening, so Tempranillo keeps acidity and the wines are built for long ageing.

Soils are clay-limestone, ferrous red clays and stony alluvial terraces along the rivers. Haro's Barrio de la Estación, where López de Heredia, CVNE, La Rioja Alta, Muga, Bilbaínas and Roda stand side by side, is the symbol of classic Rioja, and the zone's long-aged Reservas and Gran Reservas defined the region's style in the twentieth century. Labels may name the zona only when all the grapes come from it.
es-rioja-alta.terroir: Clay-limestone, ferrous clay and alluvial terraces; Atlantic-influenced climate, the coolest of the three zones.

es-rioja-andosilla.name: Andosilla
es-rioja-andosilla.grapes: Tempranillo, Garnacha, Graciano, Mazuelo, Viura and others
es-rioja-andosilla.classification: Vino de municipio of DOCa Rioja: since 2017 a wine may name its municipality if all the grapes come from it and it is made there.
es-rioja-andosilla.summary: Andosilla is a municipality of Rioja Oriental in Navarra, on the Ega near its confluence with the Ebro, about 9 km north of Calahorra. Its land spans roughly 300 to 440 m. Its vineyards share the warm, dry climate of Rioja Oriental, the traditional home of Garnacha.

es-rioja-anguciana.name: Anguciana
es-rioja-anguciana.grapes: Tempranillo, Garnacha, Graciano, Mazuelo, Viura and others
es-rioja-anguciana.classification: Vino de municipio of DOCa Rioja: since 2017 a wine may name its municipality if all the grapes come from it and it is made there.
es-rioja-anguciana.summary: Anguciana is a municipality of Rioja Alta in La Rioja, where the Oja meets the Tirón, just south-west of Haro. Its land spans roughly 470 to 490 m. Its vineyards share the Atlantic-influenced climate of Rioja Alta, which favours long-lived, fresh Tempranillo.

es-rioja-aras.name: Aras
es-rioja-aras.grapes: Tempranillo, Garnacha, Graciano, Mazuelo, Viura and others
es-rioja-aras.classification: Vino de municipio of DOCa Rioja: since 2017 a wine may name its municipality if all the grapes come from it and it is made there.
es-rioja-aras.summary: Aras is a municipality of Rioja Oriental in Navarra, in the hills north of Viana, about 13 km north-east of Logroño. Its land spans roughly 560 to 780 m. Its vineyards share the warm, dry climate of Rioja Oriental, the traditional home of Garnacha.

es-rioja-arenzana-de-abajo.name: Arenzana de Abajo
es-rioja-arenzana-de-abajo.grapes: Tempranillo, Garnacha, Graciano, Mazuelo, Viura and others
es-rioja-arenzana-de-abajo.classification: Vino de municipio of DOCa Rioja: since 2017 a wine may name its municipality if all the grapes come from it and it is made there.
es-rioja-arenzana-de-abajo.summary: Arenzana de Abajo is a municipality of Rioja Alta in La Rioja, in the Najerilla valley south of Nájera. Its land spans roughly 520 to 700 m. Like the rest of Rioja Alta, it grows mainly Tempranillo with some Garnacha, Mazuelo, Graciano and Viura.

es-rioja-arenzana-de-arriba.name: Arenzana de Arriba
es-rioja-arenzana-de-arriba.grapes: Tempranillo, Garnacha, Graciano, Mazuelo, Viura and others
es-rioja-arenzana-de-arriba.classification: Vino de municipio of DOCa Rioja: since 2017 a wine may name its municipality if all the grapes come from it and it is made there.

es-rioja-oriental.name: Rioja Oriental
es-rioja-oriental.grapes: Tempranillo, Garnacha, Graciano, Mazuelo, Viura and others
es-rioja-oriental.classification: Zona of DOCa Rioja: one of three zones that may appear on labels (rules of 2017, labels from 2018), for wines made entirely from grapes of that zone.
es-rioja-oriental.summary:
Rioja Oriental, called Rioja Baja until 2018, is the eastern zone: 49 municipalities of La Rioja and Navarra downstream from Logroño to Alfaro, plus the valleys of the Leza, Jubera, Cidacos and Alhama. The climate is the warmest and driest of the region, with a strong Mediterranean influence, and much of the land is low alluvial plain, though vineyards also climb to 600 to 700 m on the slopes of the Sierra de Yerga and the Cidacos valley.

Garnacha was the traditional grape here and still gives some of the zone's most distinctive wines, from old vines on the Yerga; Tempranillo now dominates. The renaming in 2018 was meant to shed the idea that 'Baja' meant lower quality, and estates such as Palacios Remondo in Alfaro have shown what its Garnacha can do.
es-rioja-oriental.terroir: Alluvial plains and terraces along the Ebro, clay and limestone on the slopes; warm, dry Mediterranean climate.

Its land spans roughly 530 to 730 m. Its vineyards share the Atlantic-influenced climate of Rioja Alta, which favours long-lived, fresh Tempranillo.

es-rioja-tricio.name: Tricio
es-rioja-tricio.grapes: Tempranillo, Garnacha, Graciano, Mazuelo, Viura and others
es-rioja-tricio.classification: Vino de municipio of DOCa Rioja: since 2017 a wine may name its municipality if all the grapes come from it and it is made there.
es-rioja-tricio.summary: Tricio is a municipality of Rioja Alta in La Rioja, beside Nájera on the Najerilla. Its land spans roughly 510 to 580 m. Its vineyards share the Atlantic-influenced climate of Rioja Alta, which favours long-lived, fresh Tempranillo. The Roman town of Tritium Magallum stood here; the hermitage of Santa María de Arcos reuses Roman columns.

es-rioja-tudelilla.name: Tudelilla
es-rioja-tudelilla.grapes: Tempranillo, Garnacha, Graciano, Mazuelo, Viura and others
es-rioja-tudelilla.classification: Vino de municipio of DOCa Rioja: since 2017 a wine may name its municipality if all the grapes come from it and it is made there.
es-rioja-tudelilla.summary: Tudelilla is a municipality of Rioja Oriental in La Rioja, on the slopes between the Cidacos and the Ebro, about 7 km north of Arnedo. Its land spans roughly 450 to 700 m. Rioja Oriental is warmer and drier, with Garnacha as the traditional grape and Tempranillo now dominant. Recognised viñedos singulares include Montepedriza and Proelio Los Aldares.

es-rioja-urunuela.name: Uruñuela
es-rioja-urunuela.grapes: Tempranillo, Garnacha, Graciano, Mazuelo, Viura and others
es-rioja-urunuela.classification: Vino de municipio of DOCa Rioja: since 2017 a wine may name its municipality if all the grapes come from it and it is made there.
es-rioja-urunuela.summary: Uruñuela is a municipality of Rioja Alta in La Rioja, in the lower Najerilla valley, about 5 km north-east of Nájera. Its land spans roughly 450 to 550 m. Its vineyards share the Atlantic-influenced climate of Rioja Alta, which favours long-lived, fresh Tempranillo. Bodegas Leza García is based here. Recognised viñedos singulares include Sínodo Raposeras, Sínodo Centales, Los Topos by Leza García and Los Natos de Leza García.

es-rioja-ventosa.name: Ventosa
es-rioja-ventosa.grapes: Tempranillo, Garnacha, Graciano, Mazuelo, Viura and others
es-rioja-ventosa.classification: Vino de municipio of DOCa Rioja: since 2017 a wine may name its municipality if all the grapes come from it and it is made there.
es-rioja-ventosa.summary: Ventosa is a municipality of Rioja Alta in La Rioja, on the Camino de Santiago between Navarrete and Nájera. Its land spans roughly 610 to 860 m. In Rioja Alta, the coolest and most Atlantic of the three zones, Tempranillo dominates on clay-limestone and alluvial soils.

es-rioja-viana.name: Viana
es-rioja-viana.grapes: Tempranillo, Garnacha, Graciano, Mazuelo, Viura and others
es-rioja-viana.classification: Vino de municipio of DOCa Rioja: since 2017 a wine may name its municipality if all the grapes come from it and it is made there.
es-rioja-viana.summary: Viana is a municipality of Rioja Oriental in Navarra, on the Camino de Santiago facing Logroño. Its land spans roughly 360 to 580 m. In the Mediterranean-influenced Rioja Oriental, Tempranillo and Garnacha ripen fully, giving generous, supple wines. Cesare Borgia, killed nearby in 1507, is buried at the church of Santa María. Recognised viñedos singulares include Agrum and La Escaleruela.

es-rioja-villabuena-de-alava.name: Villabuena de Álava
es-rioja-villabuena-de-alava.grapes: Tempranillo, Garnacha, Graciano, Mazuelo, Viura and others
es-rioja-villabuena-de-alava.classification: Vino de municipio of DOCa Rioja: since 2017 a wine may name its municipality if all the grapes come from it and it is made there.
es-rioja-villabuena-de-alava.summary: Villabuena de Álava is a municipality of Rioja Alavesa in Álava, on the terraces between the sierra and the Ebro, about 7 km west of Laguardia. Its land spans roughly 460 to 540 m. As across Rioja Alavesa, Tempranillo dominates on pale clay-limestone, much of it farmed by small family growers. It has one of the highest numbers of wineries per inhabitant in Spain; Luis Cañas and Izadi are based here. Recognised viñedos singulares include El Regalo, Finca El Palacio, El Regollar, Ribagaitas, Camino Leza, El Orgullo de Julián, El Cuartillo de Araico, Finca El Ribazo and Alto los Muertos Bideona.

es-rioja-villalba-de-rioja.name: Villalba de Rioja
es-rioja-villalba-de-rioja.grapes: Tempranillo, Garnacha, Graciano, Mazuelo, Viura and others
es-rioja-villalba-de-rioja.classification: Vino de municipio of DOCa Rioja: since 2017 a wine may name its municipality if all the grapes come from it and it is made there.
es-rioja-villalba-de-rioja.summary: Villalba de Rioja is a municipality of Rioja Alta in La Rioja, in the foothills of the Montes Obarenes north-west of Haro. Its land spans roughly 500 to 780 m. In Rioja Alta, the coolest and most Atlantic of the three zones, Tempranillo dominates on clay-limestone and alluvial soils.

es-rioja-villamediana-de-iregua.name: Villamediana de Iregua
es-rioja-villamediana-de-iregua.grapes: Tempranillo, Garnacha, Graciano, Mazuelo, Viura and others
es-rioja-villamediana-de-iregua.classification: Vino de municipio of DOCa Rioja: since 2017 a wine may name its municipality if all the grapes come from it and it is made there.
es-rioja-villamediana-de-iregua.summary: Villamediana de Iregua is a municipality of Rioja Oriental in La Rioja, in the lower Iregua valley next to Logroño. Its land spans roughly 390 to 500 m. Its vineyards share the warm, dry climate of Rioja Oriental, the traditional home of Garnacha. Recognised viñedo singular: Sínodo Los Tollos.

es-rioja-villar-de-torre.name: Villar de Torre
es-rioja-villar-de-torre.grapes: Tempranillo, Garnacha, Graciano, Mazuelo, Viura and others
es-rioja-villar-de-torre.classification: Vino de municipio of DOCa Rioja: since 2017 a wine may name its municipality if all the grapes come from it and it is made there.
es-rioja-villar-de-torre.summary: Villar de Torre is a municipality of Rioja Alta in La Rioja, in the foothills of the Sierra de la Demanda, about 11 km south-east of Santo Domingo de la Calzada. Its land spans roughly 690 to 1140 m. In Rioja Alta, the coolest and most Atlantic of the three zones, Tempranillo dominates on clay-limestone and alluvial soils.

es-rioja-villarejo.name: Villarejo
es-rioja-villarejo.grapes: Tempranillo, Garnacha, Graciano, Mazuelo, Viura and others
es-rioja-villarejo.classification: Vino de municipio of DOCa Rioja: since 2017 a wine may name its municipality if all the grapes come from it and it is made there.
es-rioja-villarejo.summary: Villarejo is a municipality of Rioja Alta in La Rioja, in the foothills of the Sierra de la Demanda, about 9 km south-east of Santo Domingo de la Calzada. Its land spans roughly 740 to 1220 m. Like the rest of Rioja Alta, it grows mainly Tempranillo with some Garnacha, Mazuelo, Graciano and Viura.

es-rioja-villarroya.name: Villarroya
es-rioja-villarroya.grapes: Tempranillo, Garnacha, Graciano, Mazuelo, Viura and others
es-rioja-villarroya.classification: Vino de municipio of DOCa Rioja: since 2017 a wine may name its municipality if all the grapes come from it and it is made there.
es-rioja-villarroya.summary: Villarroya is a municipality of Rioja Oriental in La Rioja, high in the hills south of Arnedo. Its land spans roughly 820 to 1040 m. Its vineyards share the warm, dry climate of Rioja Oriental, the traditional home of Garnacha.

es-rioja-yecora.name: Yécora
es-rioja-yecora.grapes: Tempranillo, Garnacha, Graciano, Mazuelo, Viura and others
es-rioja-yecora.classification: Vino de municipio of DOCa Rioja: since 2017 a wine may name its municipality if all the grapes come from it and it is made there.
es-rioja-yecora.summary: Yécora is a municipality of Rioja Alavesa in Álava, in the eastern part of Rioja Alavesa, about 9 km north of Logroño. Its land spans roughly 480 to 710 m. Rioja Alavesa's chalky clay-limestone and the shelter of the sierra give fine, perfumed Tempranillo.

es-rioja-zarraton.name: Zarratón
es-rioja-zarraton.grapes: Tempranillo, Garnacha, Graciano, Mazuelo, Viura and others
es-rioja-zarraton.classification: Vino de municipio of DOCa Rioja: since 2017 a wine may name its municipality if all the grapes come from it and it is made there.
es-rioja-zarraton.summary: Zarratón is a municipality of Rioja Alta in La Rioja, on the plateau south of Haro. Its land spans roughly 520 to 590 m. Its vineyards share the Atlantic-influenced climate of Rioja Alta, which favours long-lived, fresh Tempranillo.
